questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the engine running and the vehicle in gear.
Do the check from inside the vehicle.
Check the lights using a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.explanation: To check your lights, set the parking brake and turn off the engine. Remove the key from the ignition and take it with you. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out of the vehicle to check that all lights are working.

questions.question: You must put out emergency warning devices within ____ of stopping on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the shoulder of a road, put out your emergency warning devices within 10 minutes. Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you pull off the road.

questions.question: A bus driver must:

options.text: Only wear a seat belt if passengers have seat belts.
Not wear a seat belt, but should be encouraged to do so.

questions.explanation: Bus driver seats have seat belts. A driver must always wear a seat belt while driving a bus.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake wear. The four basic types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, watch the gauges. Oil pressure should rise to normal within a few seconds.

questions.question: The drive shaft should:

options.text: Be bent toward the passenger side.
Be bent toward the driver's side.

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check that the drive shaft is not bent or cracked.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill, what happens to your speed?

options.text: You will slow to a stop.

questions.explanation: When driving downhill, gravity causes your speed to increase.

questions.question: When driving through a curve during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Leave your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Slow down after entering the curve.
Not look for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve, reduce your speed enough so you don't need to brake or shift while turning. Stay in your lane and keep checking for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: While driving, watch the road ahead for hazards. Plan how you would handle any dangers if they occur.

questions.question: If an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) breaks down, what happens?

options.text: A yellow warning light will appear on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow warning light will appear on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have a yellow warning light on the dashboard. This light turns on if the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: A person working on a disabled vehicle on the road shoulder:

options.text: Will likely pay attention to traffic on the road.
May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on disabled vehicles. They may be concentrating on repairs and might not notice traffic or other dangers.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing has no warning gates or lights, you should:

options.text: Not worry because the tracks are likely abandoned.
Park your vehicle and walk to the tracks to check for trains.
Look both ways down the tracks to check for approaching trains.
Do what the other vehicles around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both ways down the tracks to check for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing without gates or lights is called a passive crossing. Before crossing, look down the tracks in both directions to make sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the drinks were consumed

questions.explanation: Three main factors affect blood alcohol concentration: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the person's weight. Drink temperature does not matter.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Help drivers see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles use curved convex mirrors. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away in convex mirrors than they really are.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless carrying hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless traveling through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective warning triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: A burning tire should be:
questions.explanation: Cool a burning tire with water. You may need to use large amounts of water to fully cool the tire.

questions.question: When it is hard to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, you can help other drivers by:

options.text: Waving your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When it is hard to see, turn on your headlights. If you cannot see other vehicles clearly, they probably cannot see you clearly either.

questions.question: If there are two left turn lanes, which one should you use?

options.text: Large vehicles should not turn where there are two left turn lanes.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to turn left. If there are two left turn lanes, use the right one to begin your turn.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like the road is just wet.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:

options.text: Not recommended because it can damage the vehicle.
Not recommended because it may confuse other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can hurt your vehicle's engine and parts.
